title: feat: add Jev context-trimmer agent
author: ale-rls
pr_body_excerpt:
Fixes #15723

- Adds a self-contained context-trimmer agent: Jev scores archived outputs; Nano answers using retained strings verbatim. Invalid decisions stop generation.
- Keeps the upstream submission to `agent.ts`, `agent.test.mjs`, `code-agent.json` and a short README, following maintainer feedback. Full tooling and evidence remain in [the public source repository](https://github.com/ale-rls/jev-context-trimmer).
- Callable model: `community/ale-rls/jev-context-trimmer` (private, owner-callable).
- Three deployed-agent runs on 2026-09-30 produced different real decisions:

| Task | Billing probability | Weather probability | Retained output |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Billing | 0.98 | 0.02 | billing_test |
| Weather | 0.01 | 0.96 | paris_forecast |
| Unrelated | 0.01 | 0.01 | none |

- Exact retained strings and expected selections passed live assertions; observed cost approximately 0.000333 Quest Pollen. [Full evidence](https://github.com/ale-rls/jev-context-trimmer/blob/main/EVIDENCE.md).
- Cleanup validation: eight tests pass on Node 24; request example parses; whitespace check passes. Runtime, tests and deployment config are unchanged. Original strict TypeScript and Biome checks passed before submission.

gist.headline: Jev keeps the useful scraps
gist.blurb: ale-rls built an agent that sorts archived outputs before Nano answers. Billing notes stay for billing questions, forecasts stay for weather questions, and unrelated clutter stays out of the way.
gist.summary: ale-rls added the private, owner-callable `community/ale-rls/jev-context-trimmer` agent, where Jev selects relevant archived outputs and Nano answers with retained strings verbatim, halting generation on invalid decisions.
gist.impact: The owner can call the agent to retain `billing_test` for billing tasks, `paris_forecast` for weather tasks, or nothing for unrelated tasks, as demonstrated in three deployed-agent runs.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Jev's context trimming as a small sorting desk for archived output cards: a billing card and a weather card go into separate labeled flower pots, while irrelevant cards remain on the shelf. Polli helps sort the cards; a friendly CRT monitor represents Nano reading only the selected card. Jev and Nano have no specified mascots or logos, so use labeled tools rather than invented characters.
